home.eyebrow: Oldest city in Germany - UNESCO World Heritage
home.heroBody: From Porta Nigra (the Black Gate) to Trier Cathedral, from the Roman Amphitheater to the Olewig (a wine village within Trier) vineyards. Trier-Reisen is your city guide for UNESCO World Heritage, Mosel wine and Roman heritage.
home.unescoBody: Eight UNESCO sites within a few square kilometers. These six landmarks anchor every trip to Trier.
home.districtsBody: From the UNESCO old town to the wine village of Olewig, from the Moselle promenade to the university district of Kürenz.
home.upcomingBody: Antikenfestspiele (Roman theater festival), Olewiger Weinfest (wine festival) and the Christmas market: Trier's major events.

hotelEvent.mapLead: Every hotel in this part of Trier with live rates. Zoom and pan to compare locations before you book.
hotelEvent.orientationBody: Trier sits in the far west of Germany, on the Mosel (Moselle) river and close to the Luxembourg border. Most visitors coming from the US fly into Frankfurt and drive the rest of the way, roughly two hours by car. The old town itself is compact and walkable: Porta Nigra (the Black Gate), the Hauptmarkt (the main market square), the Cathedral of St. Peter and the Roman baths all sit within a few hundred meters of one another, so nearly any hotel in the center leaves the UNESCO sites within walking distance.
hotelEvent.neighborhoodsHeading: Which part of Trier to book
hotelEvent.neighborhoodsBody: The Innenstadt (city center) is the default choice: pedestrian streets, restaurants and four UNESCO sites on foot. Olewig, a wine village that belongs to Trier, makes sense when wine is the point of the trip, and it is where the Olewiger Weinfest is held. Along the Mosel promenade you trade a few extra minutes of walking for river views and quieter nights. Hotels on the southern edge of the old town are typically about a ten-minute walk from the Hauptmarkt.
